_why_no_T: JSON has no comment syntax and `Recipe` does not deny unknown fields, so this
array is how this file records a decision a reader would otherwise have to guess
at. It is data nothing reads.
The disc's `OS-Version3.9/Workbench3.5` holds 16 top-level drawers; the rules
below place 14. `T` and `WBStartup` are the two left out, and both are
deliberate rather than overlooked:
`T` is AmigaDOS's temporary directory, and on a running 3.9 system it is not
on SYS: at all. Measured on the owner's own AmigaOS39.iso (2026-08-19): the
disc's own `S/Startup-Sequence` — the file this recipe *does* place — runs
`C:MakeDir RAM:T RAM:Clipboards RAM:ENV RAM:ENV/Sys` and then
`Assign >NIL: T: RAM:T`, so `T:` is made in RAM at every boot and the disc's
copy is never consulted. The disc's `T` drawer is also empty (0 entries, by
7-Zip). AmigaOS 3.2's tree, which ART built and which booted to a clean
Workbench under WinUAE, likewise carries no `T` and its own Startup-Sequence
does the identical two lines. Copying an empty drawer whose assign points
elsewhere would place a directory the system never looks at.
`WBStartup` belongs to the second, unwritten half of this recipe rather than
to `workbench-base`: it is where a system's own startup programs are chosen,
and which ones a 3.9 tree should carry is one of the things the boot test
(spec section 4) was meant to establish and did not, because no 3.9 tree has
been booted yet.
If a boot disagrees with either judgement, add the rule then, with the run as
the reason — that is what a real run is for.
_why_locale_base_ART_162: Added in a Task 4 review fix round, not the round that first wrote this
file — filed as ART-162. The disc carries a whole second top-level drawer,
sibling to `Workbench3.5`, this recipe placed nothing from at all:
`OS-Version3.9/Locale` (Catalogs, Countries, Flags, Help, Languages,
Providers — measured with `7z l -slt` against the owner's own
AmigaOS39.iso). Without it, `locale.library` has no `.language` or
`.country` file to select *any* non-English locale by — not just Turkish,
every one of them — which is what made the `locale-turkish` package (this
same task) inert: its 36 catalogs would sit on the volume with nothing
that could ever pick the language they translate.
Four of the six drawers are taken: `Catalogs`, `Countries`, `Languages`,
`Help` — the set `locale.library`'s own selection actually reads
(Locale prefs picks a `.country`/`.language` pair and points programs at
`Locale:Catalogs/<language>/*.catalog`). `Flags` (globe icons for the
Locale prefs country picker) and `Providers` (dial-up ISP presets for
Miami-era internet software this project does not install) are left out
**of this component**, whose scope is locale *selection*.
**Corrected in Task 8, fix round 2 (F3).** What stood here said they
were left out as `cosmetic/unrelated`, which reads as a judgement that
they are unwanted on the volume. They are not, and as of ART-169 they
ship: `workbench-39` places `OS-VERSION3.9/WORKBENCH3.9/LOCALE` whole,
and its 61 `Flags` rows (Countries **and** a whole `Keymaps` set, only
16 of which this component's own source even has) and 4 `Providers`
reach the volume through it. That is accepted and intended — both are
part of AmigaOS 3.9. The exclusion here was always about *this*
component's scope, never about the files, and the two components are
complementary rather than overlapping on this point: `locale-base` is
the only source of any catalog or `.language` on the disc, and
`workbench-39` is the only source of `Flags` and `Providers`. See that
component's own `_why_overrides_and_why_last` for the measured
per-drawer comparison.
`required: false`, matching the shipped AmigaOS 3.2 recipe's own
`locale-base` component exactly (`recipes/amigaos-3.2.json`): a system
with no Locale tree still boots and runs in English, the ROM's own
default — nothing analogous to `install-libs`'s missing `icon.library`
forces this one on.

_why_rom_at_least_40: ART-157. The recipe format could state a Kickstart *maximum*
(`rom-older-than`, which 3.2 uses to add `modules-a1200` back for a
pre-V47 ROM) and not a minimum, so AmigaOS 3.9's own requirement went
unstated and unchecked. Approximating it through `rom-older-than`
would have asserted something false, which is why it was filed rather
than invented.
**The number is the disc's own, read off the artefact rather than
recalled.** `OS-Version3.9/OS3.9Install` — the release's own Installer
script, `$VER: Install 45.0 (24.11.2000)` — carries the refusal string
`#bad-kick`:
You have to install Kickstart 3.1 ROMs before installing
Workbench 3.9.
and, in the German catalogue beside it, `Sie müssen Kickstart 3.1 und
min. Workbench 3.0 zur Nutzung von Workbench 3.9 vorinstallieren.`
Kickstart 3.1 is V40, so 40 is the floor the release itself names.
(Extracted from the owner's own AmigaOS39.iso with 7-Zip, 2026-08-20.
The manual's `installation/book-main1.html` states the *hardware*
floor — 68020, 6 MB Chip and 4 MB Fast on pre-A1200 models — and no
Kickstart version at all, which is why the installer and not the
manual is cited here.)
**Declared on `workbench-base`, which is `required`, so it is a
statement and not a switch.** A `Condition` can only ever turn a
component *on* (`plan::resolve_components_on`), and this one is on
regardless; what the declaration changes is what the finished tree
records. `plan::rom_requirement` reads it into
`PairedRom::requires_major`, and that is what G9's
`core::rom::pairing::compare` puts to the card's own Kickstart before
the destructive step runs — a card carrying a V37 or V39 ROM now
reports `Unsuitable { needs: 40 }` instead of nothing at all.
One thing this deliberately does **not** do: refuse to build the tree.
A 3.9 tree is assembled on the host and the Kickstart it will meet is
the card's, which may not be the one paired at plan time — and may not
exist yet. The requirement is recorded and checked where it can
actually be acted on.

_why_a_second_layer_and_not_a_bigger_wor: ART-169, and the first thing to say is what this component is *not*:
it is not a correction of `workbench-base`'s source. Both trees are
real and neither is a complete volume. Measured with `7z l -slt`
against the owner's own AmigaOS39.iso (2026-08-19):
OS-Version3.9/Workbench3.5   673 rows, 16 drawers
OS-Version3.9/Workbench3.9   854 rows, 13 drawers
`Workbench3.9` has no `L`, no `Expansion`, no `Rexxc` and no `T`; its
own `S` holds `bg`, `fg`, `fork`, `SetFont`, `SetKeyboard`, `History`
and three ARexx scripts and **no `Startup-Sequence`**; and there is no
`Workbench3.9/C/Version` at all. Its `C` holds 29 commands where 3.5's
holds 52, and 12 of the 29 are replacements while 17 are new. Its
`Libs/workbench.library` is 199,852 bytes against 3.5's 193,400 — a
different, larger file, not the same one twice.
So `Workbench3.9` ships only what changed, which is exactly why a 3.9
CD carries a `Workbench3.5` drawer at all: the real Installer lays 3.5
and then lays 3.9 over it. `workbench-base` was never installing the
wrong tree — it was stopping after the first layer, which is why the
tree booted clean (ART-169's own evidence) while reporting
`Workbench 44.5` and failing `C:LoadMonDrvs` on the first line of the
Startup-Sequence it *did* place. The Startup-Sequence in
`Workbench3.5/S` is already the 3.9 one; the command it calls lives
only in this layer.
The rules below are read off the disc's own `Workbench3.9` drawer
listing, **not** copied from `workbench-base` — the two lists differ by
five drawers in each direction, and copying one recipe's rule list into
another is the mistake BoingBag 3.9-2's own JSON records nearly making.
_why_overrides_and_why_last: `plan()` emits items in recipe-declaration order and `apply`'s writer
lets the last writer win, so an overlay has to be declared *after* the
layers it covers. It is last in this array for that reason and no
other.
`overrides` names both, because both are really collided with:
workbench-base — 12 of this layer's 29 `C` commands replace a 3.5
command of the same name, and every other drawer overlaps the same
way. `detect_collisions` refuses an undeclared claim outright, so
this is load-bearing rather than documentary.
locale-base — measured, not assumed. `Workbench3.9/Locale` and
`OS-Version3.9/Locale` are *overlapping and complementary*, and
neither contains the other:
Countries  32 of 33 shared (locale-base carries one more)
Catalogs   this layer's drawer is EMPTY; locale-base has 645
Languages  this layer's drawer is EMPTY; locale-base has 22
Help       disjoint: this layer has only ViNCEd.guide(+.info),
the 3.9 console handler's guide; locale-base has 45
other guides and not that one
Flags      61 here (Countries *and* a whole Keymaps set) against
locale-base's 20, only 16 shared
Providers  4, identical
So `locale-base` is not redundant — it is the only source of any
catalog or any `.language` file, which is what ART-162 added it
for — and this layer is not redundant either.
One consequence stated rather than left to be discovered: this rule
places `Locale` whole, so `Locale/Flags` (61 rows) and
`Locale/Providers` (4) reach the volume, and `locale-base` places
neither. **Ruled on in Task 8, fix round 2 (F3): shipping them is
accepted.** Both are part of AmigaOS 3.9, and `locale-base`'s own
note excluded them because they are outside *that* component's
scope — locale selection — not because anything judged them
unwanted. That note has been corrected to say so from its side too,
so the two read together rather than contradicting each other.
